chunks: Ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, peace be upon him) about a man who sought the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) for a piece of land, and it was agreed that he would bring the money, but he did not arrive. So what should the owner of the land do if he wishes to sell it? Should he sell it or wait for the arrival of his partner, the owner of the right of pre-emption? He said: 'If he is in the city, the owner should wait with him for three days. If he comes with the money, then [the sale is valid with him]; otherwise, he should sell it and his right of pre-emption in the land is nullified. And if he requested a delay until he could bring the money from one town to another, the owner should wait for him for the duration of the man's travel to that town, plus an additional three days upon his arrival. If he meets him [with the money], then [the sale is valid with him]; otherwise, he has no right of pre-emption.'

key_terms.بَطَلَتْ شُفْعَتُهُ: His right of pre-emption is nullified/voided.
key_terms.بِالْمِصْرِ: In the city or local area.
key_terms.شُفْعَة: Right of pre-emption; the right of a partner or co-owner to buy out the other's share before selling to an outsider.

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a partner exercising the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) if they are delayed in bringing the money?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural mechanics of *shuf'ah* (pre-emption), a right deeply rooted in pre-Islamic Arab custom and codified in Shia jurisprudence to prevent harm from unexpected co-ownership. It establishes a fair grace period based on the pre-emptor's distance, balancing the owner's need for liquidity with the pre-emptor's right of first refusal, thereby ensuring transactional certainty. The ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical equity (*adl*) in commercial law, ensuring that the right is not lost due to minor delays but is not indefinitely suspended either.
